Apple has disclosed how its new Siri AI features will operate for users in China. These new AI features will be powered by Alibaba's Qwen model.

Although the iPhone maker partners with Google in most countries, using its Gemini model, the Chinese government requires Apple to work with a local AI company instead...

In most countries, the new Siri AI features are powered by Google's Gemini model. These features run on Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers, or on Apple-exclusive servers provided by Google, with specific protections in place for Siri AI users. These include privacy requirements similar to those of the PCC servers, ensuring that neither Apple nor Google can access user interactions.

However, in China, the law only permits the use of Chinese AI models. This is likely to allow the government to monitor usage, so the same privacy safeguards should not apply.

Reuters reports that Apple has published a guide stating that the new features will rely on Alibaba's Qwen model. The guide is for Mac, but the report says iPhone, iPad, and Vision Pro will all use the same model.

There is one fairly clear indication that privacy protections will not apply in the same way: Reuters notes that Mac users will need to have their own Qwen account and must be logged in.
